To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

globalization, in aggregate and on average tends toward reducing the autonomy and capacity, although not necessarily the influence, of states, but that globalization affects the relative power and influence of states differently, and thus affects the balance of international power.

(1) globalization, on average and in the aggregate, reduces the autonomy and capacity (relative power) of states, but (2) globalization also affects the balance of relative power between states, so that some states are more adversely affected than others; and (3) because of its size, wealth, and location, the United States is the biggest winner in a more open and globalized world.

(1) the globalization process is not uniform, but is instead characterized by a number of different trends, each of which is likely to have different consequences for the distribution of power among states; (2) the overall impact of globalization on the distribution of power is ambiguous and depends on how globalization is measured and how the distribution of power itself is measured; and (3) the impact of globalization on American power is likely to be positive, but not necessarily in ways that are consistent with the United States

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the globalization of the world economy has been a long-term process, but it has accelerated in the last 25 years, and it is likely to continue to accelerate.
globalization has not only increased the power of the United States, but also reduced its autonomy and increased the costs of exercising power.

globalization, in aggregate and on average tends (a) to reduce the autonomy of states, but (b) to enhance their capacity, although in certain respects the reverse is also true; (c) to increase the power of the United States; and (d) to erode the power of all other states.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
globalization, while not a panacea, has been an important force for the spread of democracy, the reduction of poverty, and the promotion of human rights, and that it will remain so in the future.

globalization is a complex, multi dimensional process that is reshaping the structure of the international system, and the ways in which the United States and other states interact with each other and with the global economy and society.

the processes of globalization are transforming international politics in ways that are likely to have profound consequences for the international security of the United States.
